problem: Find a basis of the null space of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}].$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of the Null Space of a Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Basis for the Null Space of a Matrix Given in Reduced Row Echelon Form
examples.problem: Find a basis of the null space of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064941/assets/e85d4892dc0bad0c6019b0434eff3d140fcf654171f6fda480b109b324e7b443.png)
examples.worked_solution:
To find a basis of $\textrm{Null}(A),$ we need to solve the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ and express the solution as a linear combination of linearly independent vectors. Those vectors form a basis of $\textrm{Null}(A).$

The given matrix is already in reduced row echelon form. So, the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ corresponds to the following system:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064941/assets/367b1779ba31df69791a24ab485f1715cedb46f57e383053fd17a189c465d09a.png)

Here, $x_1$ and $x_3$ are basic variables corresponding to the pivot columns ($1$st and $3$rd) and $x_2,x_4$ are free variables corresponding to the non-pivot columns. Therefore, if $\mathbf{x} \in \textrm{Null}(A),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 4{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{4}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $x_2,x_4\in\mathbb{R}.$ This implies that

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064941/assets/9b2704bbd684106b7c1c7dbe52eb957e65e6634d9adb6ba7fb415b0097af7e64.png)

is a basis of $\textrm{Null}(A)$ since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate $\textrm{Null}(A).$

feedback.problem: Given that  $\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{3}\in R}$, find a basis for $\text{Null}(A).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\text{Null}(A)$ has the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Expanding, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, a basis for $\text{Null}(A)$ is

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}
$$

since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate $\text{Null}(A).$
